objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have practiced and developed the sub-skills of listening for gist and detailed comprehension in the context of parent-teen relationships and mutual influence.
materials:
- ODF Level 3, Workbook, p.9
- Audio recording 1.01

stages.stage_aim: To activate learners' interest in the theme of parent-teen relationships and set the context for the listening task
stages.procedure: Write 'Generation Gap' on the board. Elicit what Ss think it means. In pairs, Ss discuss: 'Do you and your parents see things differently? Give an example.' Brief whole-class feedback to pool ideas.

stages.stage_aim: To get the general idea of a podcast about whether parents and teens can really understand each other
stages.procedure: Ss listen to 1.01 and get the main topic. Differentiation: Stronger Ss listen without looking at the questions, take notes, then answer from notes. Core and Support Ss use the questions in their workbook as a guide. Ss compare answers in pairs, then class feedback to confirm.

stages.stage_aim: To identify specific information about what Dr. Schmidt's research reveals about parent-teen influence
stages.procedure: Ss listen to 1.01 again and complete the multiple-choice questions. Differentiation: Stronger Ss attempt to answer from memory after the first listen, then verify on the second listen. Core Ss see the options and choose while listening. Support Ss use the underlined key words strategy to focus on relevant parts. Pairs compare before class feedback.

stages.stage_aim: To notice and practise useful phrases for persuading someone
stages.procedure: Ss complete Exercise 4 (complete the dialogue with phrases a-g). Differentiation: Stronger Ss cover the phrase bank first and attempt from memory, then check. Core Ss match phrases directly. Support Ss have a reduced set of 3-4 phrases to choose from. Pairs check answers. Elicit key phrases onto the board.

stages.stage_aim: To practise using persuasion phrases spontaneously in a structured speaking line-up
stages.procedure: Two lines of Ss face each other. Each pair receives a topic. Ss have 1-2 minutes to persuade their partner using phrases from Exercise 4 — no notes allowed. After each round, one line rotates so Ss face a new partner with a new topic. Repeat for 6 topics. Teacher monitors and takes notes for delayed error correction.
